title: Graphs of Exponential and Logarithmic Functions
seo_title: Algebra II Exponential and Logarithmic Functions Worksheets (TEKS 2A.5A)
domain: Exponential and Logarithmic Functions and Equations
standard_text: 2A.5A determine the effects on the key attributes on the graphs of f(x) = b^x and f(x) = log_b(x) where b is 2, 10, and e when f(x) is replaced by af(x), f(x) + d, and f(x − c) for specific positive and negative real values of a, c, and d
meta_desc: Free Algebra II worksheets for Texas TEKS 2A.5A: transformations of exponential and logarithmic graphs with bases 2, 10 and e, asymptotes, domain, range, growth and decay. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: b^(x − c) + d has asymptote y = d; log_b(x − c) + d has asymptote x = c.
key_sub: A negative a reflects the graph over the x-axis.
body_html:
How to think about it

  • g(x) = a · bx − c + d: the horizontal asymptote moves to y = d.
  • g(x) = a logb(x − c) + d: the vertical asymptote moves to x = c, and the domain is x > c.
  • A negative a reflects the graph over the x-axis; for an exponential the range becomes y < d.
  • log means base 10 and ln means base e ≈ 2.718.

Examples

Example

g(x) = 2x + 3 − 4

Left 3, down 4

Asymptote y = −4

Answer: Range y > −4

Example

g(x) = ln(x − 5)

Right 5

Answer: Asymptote x = 5, domain x > 5

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Shifting the wrong wayx − 3 moves right 3.
Moving the horizontal asymptote with cOnly d moves y = 0.
Mixing up domain and rangeLogs limit the domain; exponentials limit the range.

A number about 2.718 used for continuous growth.

faq.q: Are b^x and log_b x related?
faq.a: Yes. They are inverses, reflections of each other over y = x.

faq.q: Does a log graph have a horizontal asymptote?
faq.a: No. It has a vertical asymptote.
